Subject: Post-demo: geo performance plan + hyperscaler comparison (next steps)

Hi Sam --

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap of what we covered on the call and proposed next steps so we have everything in one place.

What we heard from you:
- Primary workload: patient-facing summarization & secure retrieval for EHR snippets (p95 token length ~120).
- Latency SLO: interactive experience <= 250ms p95 for US and EU regions; APAC is lower priority but a blocker for pilots.
- Compliance: EU data residency and SOC 2 evidence required prior to pilot kick-off.
- Competitive concern: you're evaluating both hyperscaler managed endpoints (AWS Bedrock / Azure OpenAI) and a self-hosted inference route.

How Redwood fits (high level):
- Lower run-to-run variance: our unified serving runtime + smart routing reduces p99 spikes vs naive managed endpoints.
- Cost options: dedicated pools and quantized model variants to close cost gaps with hyperscalers at scale.
- Data controls: Private deployment (VPC) with KMS integration to address residency + auditability.

Immediate next steps we propose:
1) Technical geo-sweep (we'll run request-level latency tests from US-EAST, EU-WEST, APAC-TOKYO and provide p50/p95/p99 and throughput at 1/5/10 qps).
2) Competitive apples-to-apples: we'll run the same prompt set (you provided sample prompts) against your Bedrock trial and our hosted endpoint so you can compare tail-latency and token cost.
3) Compliance packet: Laura will attach SOC 2 artifacts and our Private deployment checklist.
4) MAP: we'll send a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with dates for tests, pilot acceptance criteria, and commercialization steps.

Can you confirm the test window you prefer next week (Mon/Tue morning ET works for us)? Also confirm whether we should include an APAC target (Tokyo) in the initial sweep or keep it US/EU only.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: benchmark_results_template.csv (CSV template for latency/cost results), mutual_action_plan_NBH_v1.pdf (draft MAP)

Neha --

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: we can run the Bedrock trial but we don't want to expose PHI outside our VPC for the pilot, so please treat the trial prompts as pseudonymized -- we'll provide a masked dataset.

Test window: Tue morning ET (Feb 24) is best for our infra team. Please include APAC (Tokyo) -- one of our clinics in Singapore will be part of the pilot and we want to see real-world latency there.

For acceptance criteria, the short list:
- p95 <= 250ms (US/EU) with <1.5x cost per token of our current managed spend for the same model quality.
- Clear fallback if a region is congested (we don't want a visible outage).

Also, can you confirm whether Redwood's Dedicated offering supports HIPAA BAAs? That will affect whether we run the pilot under hosted or dedicated.

--Sam

Hi Sam --

Thanks for the quick reply and the test-window confirmation. A few technical notes and the planned test matrix (high level):

Planned tests (Feb 24 morning ET):
- Geo latency sweep: 2500 requests per region (US-EAST, EU-WEST, APAC-TOKYO) at steady 1 qps, 5 qps, 10 qps. Capture p50/p95/p99, cold vs warm-starts, and KV cache hit rates.
- Hyperscaler parity run: run the masked prompt set concurrently against your Bedrock trial and our hosted endpoint to measure latency and token accounting. We'll supply a simple harness (curl + sequence-length control) to make runs comparable.
- Stress case: 100 concurrent long-context (>1k tokens) requests to measure tail behavior and memory limits.

What we need from you before the run:
1) Masked dataset (CSV) uploaded to our shared Drive folder (link below).
2) Bedrock trial credentials or short-lived API key (we can coordinate secure handoff via your vault). If you prefer, we can provide a proxy harness so keys never leave your infra.
3) Confirmation on whether to run the tests under our hosted endpoint or a short-term Dedicated instance (we can spin a 1-node Dedicated pool for the test).

On the HIPAA/BAA question: Redwood supports HIPAA-level controls in Private and Dedicated deployments; we can provide a BAA for enterprise Dedicated contracts. Hosted accounts can be configured with certain controls but most customers doing PHI choose Dedicated/Private. I'll let Laura add the compliance artifacts.

Deliverables (by EOD Feb 25):
- CSV with raw latency traces + summary plots
- Side-by-side cost comparison (tokens * unit pricing, estimated monthly run cost at projected qps)
- MAP with acceptance criteria and milestones

Drive link for upload: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cExampleDriveLink

I'll attach the benchmark template CSV now and the MAP draft shortly.

--Markus
